pages.text: $(bold)Speed Upgrade Module:$(0) makes the miner faster — and hungrier.$(br2)$(li)Each block: mining progress $(4)+12.5%$(0), energy cost $(e)+10%$(0) per tick$(li)Cap: $(4)10 blocks$(0)$(br2)Maxed out, that's rate ×2.25 at double the power draw (the base 10 energy/tick climbs to 20). Make sure the grid can feed it before you floor it.

$(bold)Fortune Upgrade Module:$(0) cures the "one ore per haul" stinginess.$(br2)$(li)Each block: $(4)+1$(0) item per haul$(li)Cap: $(4)4 blocks$(0)$(br2)Maxed out, every cycle yields a fixed $(4)5 items$(0) (the type is still rolled from the weight table). It adds no power cost — a great deal when stockpiling bulk ores like coal, iron and copper.

$(bold)Storage Upgrade Module:$(0) stretches the controller's fuel tank.$(br2)$(li)Each block: energy capacity $(4)+50%$(0) (multiplied onto the tier's base capacity)$(li)Cap: $(4)10 blocks$(0)$(br2)Maxed out, that's capacity ×6: Basic 1M → 6M, Ultimate 50M → 300M.$(br2)$(bold)Fitting them:$(0) modules are plain blocks — $(4)just place one into any U slot$(0) (upgrade-frame position), replacing an empty frame. The controller re-counts every 20 ticks, so adds and removals apply instantly. Modules don't care about tier — the same set and the same caps work on all four, and anything beyond the cap simply doesn't stack.
For the details, look back at the U-slot layout in "Miner Structure" and the performance gap in "Miner Tiers" — modules are the icing; the cake is your tier and your power grid.
